slides.title: East regional distribution center: close in 2027, or retain and optimize?

paragraphs.text: East regional distribution center: close in 2027, or retain and optimize?
CEO and board decision paper · Board meeting pre-read, November 2026
Northline Home
CEO and board
Based only on the board briefing pack (synthetic case data). All figures in US$, at 2027 volumes unless stated

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Retain and optimize East through its 2029 lease end and test the cross-dock: closing saves at most $0.10M a year, not $1.3M, and fails or cannot yet prove the board's tests
Closing East does not pay once routing and handling are counted
–	Serving East from Central nets $0.10M a year, not the $1.3M claimed, and zero at 2028 volume, before the $0.75M exit fee
–	The cross-dock costs $0.15M a year more than today: $0.60M of extra transport outweighs $0.45M of fixed cost removed
–	Optimized retention (K) is cheapest in the base case: $8.44M in 2027, $0.20–0.45M a year below either closure
Closure also breaks, or cannot yet prove, the board's binding constraints
–	Close to Central: 90.3% against the 92% contract; Central at 100% in 2027 and 108% in 2028; $1.85M one-time with its unbudgeted retrofit, against $0.9M
–	Cross-dock: 93.9% on paper, but from a six-week, non-holiday pilot with no all-ZIP definition and no promotion guarantee
–	Retain and optimize: 95.1% network rate, Central at 47% of capacity in 2028, and $0.15M one-time
Optimize now, test the cross-dock, and decide the 2029 lease at a Q3 2028 gate
–	Approve Option K and a cross-dock test capped at $0.25M through holiday 2027 and spring 2028, measured on all ZIP codes
–	Waiting avoids the $0.75M exit fee and settles whether the $0.85M minimum is extra or credited, a swing of $0.85M a year
–	Drop close-to-Central: its $5-per-order penalty makes it no cheaper than today at 2028 volume, even if Central were expanded

slides.title: We judged four designs and a deferral path on the board's four tests plus reversibility, using all-in cost and all-ZIP service

paragraphs.text: 1 Economics    2 Constraints    3 Recommended path
We judged four designs and a deferral path on the board's four tests plus reversibility, using all-in cost and all-ZIP service
Four network designs and a deferral path
Five tests: four set by the board, plus reversibility
▪	SQ, status quo: keep all three sites as they are today; the reference case
▪	K, retain and optimize: renegotiate East staffing shifts and add a transfer buffer for low-volume SKUs; saves $0.30M a year for $0.15M upfront
▪	C, close East and serve from Central: end the East lease in 2027 ($0.75M) and ship all 200k Eastern orders from Central at $13 each
▪	X, close East and use a cross-dock: a two-year third-party deal at $11 per order plus a $0.85M annual minimum
▪	D, defer (middle path): run K now, test the cross-dock through holiday peak, and decide at the 2029 lease end
▪	1 Economics: lowest all-in annual cost (transport, facility fixed cost, damage) plus one-time cost, not the CFO's carrier-only cost per shipment
▪	2 Service: at least 92% of all orders delivered within two days, network-wide, on all ZIP codes; the contracted KPI, not the ex-rural dashboard
▪	3 Capacity: Central at or below its 360k certified practical capacity in 2027 and under 2028 growth (East +10%, Central +6%)
▪	4 Funding and lease: no more than $0.9M of one-time change cost in 2027; East early exit $0.75M; West lease fixed to 2030
▪	5 Risk: decision-grade evidence and reversibility; rebuilding East-type capacity takes nine months
Closure is hard to reverse, so it must pass all five tests on today's evidence; a gap is a risk, not a pass
1  Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 2, 3, 6.

paragraphs.text: Refined answer
▪	Retain and optimize, not just retain: Option K beats the status quo by $0.30M a year at low risk
▪	Capacity rules out only close-to-Central: the cross-dock fails on cost, $0.45M a year above K in the base case, and on unproven peak service
▪	Keep East through 2029, not permanently: the exit fee falls away at lease end; test the cross-dock now and decide at a Q3 2028 gate
1  Source: Northline Home briefing pack (synthetic case data), sections 2–7; Northline analysis.

Reading A is the base case: the pack lists the $0.85M under fixed facility cost
▪	Reading A, a fee on top of $11 per order: the cross-dock costs more than K every year and is never worth closing East for at forecast volumes
▪	Reading B, a spend floor credited against charges: it would save $0.40M a year against K in 2027 and $0.34M in 2028, worth it only if peak all-ZIP service is proven
▪	Settle it before signing: the test contract must state whether the minimum is extra or credited

paragraphs.text: Waiting beats closing now, even under Reading B
▪	Closing in 2027 gains little: under Reading B, $0.40M + $0.34M − $0.75M exit + $0.15M of K setup avoided = $0.14M over two years
▪	Waiting avoids the early-exit fee: the lease ends in 2029, so the $0.75M charge falls away (transfer costs within it may remain)
▪	The downside is lopsided: each percentage point of Eastern service below 88.3% adds 2,000 late orders a year and pushes the network below 92%, with penalties and nine months to reverse
Close-to-Central is dropped, not deferred: it loses to K at any volume above 160k
